newsitem.title: FINLAND: OECD sees growth picking up in Finland.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees growth picking up in Finland.

text.p: The way looks clear for economic growth in Finland to pick up again in the next two years with unemployment falling faster, but the jobless rate will only decline to around 14 percent in 1998, the OECD said on Thursday.

"Low interest rates, the stable currency, improving household sentiment and a projected pick-up in world demand should pave the way for robust economic growth," the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development said.
In its biannual report, the Paris-based think tank saw some risk of inflation creeping up, but said this would remain low in a range of one to two percent.
"Unemployment aside, most economic fundamentals are reasonably strong," it said.

Finnish unemployment at around 15 percent in September is among the highest in the European Union, and the government has pledged to halve it to around eight to nine percent by the end of its term in 1999.
In August the OECD said it was unclear if Finland could meet the Maastricht criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

It made no direct comment on Finland's chances of fulfilling the criteria in its latest report, but it said the public debt-to-GDP ratio would remain just above the 60 percent EMU target ceiling, while declining modestly.
Until late November, the Finnish government had a similar outlook but it has since said it expects the ratio to be slightly below 60 percent both in 1996 and 1997.

The OECD saw Finland's general government deficit shrinking to 1.5 percent of GDP in 1996 from 2.7 percent in 1997 and further in 1998: roughly in line with less specific government forecasts. The EMU criterion is three percent.

The OECD report was compiled in early October, before the Bank of Finland made its most recent cut in the key tender rate to three percent on October 9. It makes only a passing reference to Finland joining Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism on Oct 14.
